value.rationale: The natural boundary problem is quantifying how a compact Hardy composition-adjoint product approaches its noncompact unweighted spectrum. The result resolves the exact first-order radial rate and establishes fixed-rank eigenvalue crowding, which is strictly stronger than the first numerical radius. The coefficient is arithmetic, depending on the larger coprime degree and not the smaller. The sharp spectral statement fills a motivated gap between existing unweighted finite-cutoff and damped selfcommutator theorems without claiming a general new path representation.
